title_en: Wu Lianghao v. Rugao Jinding Real Estate Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over confirmation of shareholder status
ruling_gist_en: Where the act of altering the registration of equity in a foreign-invested enterprise does not fall within the scope of the negative list management referred to in Article 4 of the Foreign Investment Law, and the parties concerned claim that the alteration of registration should be subject to the approval of the examination and approval authority for foreign-invested enterprises on the grounds that the relevant legal act occurred prior to the implementation of the Foreign Investment Law, the people's court shall not support such claim in accordance with the principles of 'national treatment' and 'equal treatment for domestic and foreign capital' as stipulated in the Foreign Investment Law.

full_text_en:
Wu Lianghao v. Rugao Jinding Real Estate Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over confirmation of shareholder qualification

Ruling Summary

Where the registration of equity change in a foreign-invested enterprise does not fall within the scope of the negative list management as referred to in Article 4 of the Foreign Investment Law, and a party claims that such change registration should have obtained the approval of the foreign-invested enterprise approval authority on the ground that the relevant legal act occurred before the implementation of the Foreign Investment Law, the people's court shall not support such claim in accordance with the principles of "national treatment" and "equal treatment of domestic and foreign investment" as provided for in the Foreign Investment Law.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2021) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 1074

Re-applicant (defendant at first instance, appellant at second instance): Rugao Jinding Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 59 Jiefang West Road, Rucheng Street, Rugao City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal representative: Feng Xueping, Chairman of the board.

Agent ad litem: Yang Mingyu, lawyer of Fujian Yebo Law Firm.

Re-applicant (third party at first instance): Nantong Zhengda Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 59 Jiefang West Road, Rucheng Street, Rugao City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal representative: Feng Xueping, Executive director.

Agent ad litem: Yang Jie, lawyer of Jiangsu Yinglian Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Feng, lawyer of Jiangsu Yinglian Law Firm.

Respondent (plaintiff at first instance, appellee at second instance): Wu Lianghao, male, born on September 26, 1951, a permanent resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, residing at House No. 8, No. 20 Tai Tam Road, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Agent ad litem: Xu Hongbing, lawyer of Jiangsu Ruyi Law Firm.

Appellant at second instance (defendant at first instance): Ye Hongbin, male, born on October 20, 1957, a permanent resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, residing at No. 18 Hanxi Dahan Lane, Hanjiang District, Putian City, Fujian Province.

Agent ad litem: Yang Mingyu, lawyer of Fujian Yebo Law Firm.

Third party at first instance: Fujian Hanjiang Dadi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at the Hanjiang Furniture Decoration Materials Market, Hanjiang District, Putian City, Fujian Province.

Legal representative: Chen Shuqin.

The re-applicants, Rugao Jinding Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinding Company) and Nantong Zhengda Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhengda Company), in the case of a dispute over confirmation of shareholder qualification with the respondent Wu Lianghao, the appellant at second instance Ye Hongbin, and the third party at first instance Fujian Hanjiang Dadi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dadi Company), applied to this Court for retrial against the civil judgment (2019) Su Min Zhong No. 1194 rendered by the Jiangsu High People's Court. This Court formed a collegiate panel in accordance with the law to conduct the review, which has now been concluded.

Jinding Company and Zhengda Company applied for retrial, alleging: (1) The equity change registration claimed by the respondent was not obtained with the consent of the foreign-invested enterprise approval authority, which does not comply with Article 14, Item (3) of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Disputes over Foreign-Invested Enterprises (I) (hereinafter referred to as the Provisions (I)), which requires that "the consent of the foreign-invested enterprise approval authority has been obtained." (2) The courts of first and second instance did not consider the opinions of Zhengda Company, and the application of law was erroneous. Zhengda Company acquired Ye Hongbin's shares in September 2018 and registered as a shareholder of Jinding Company. The relationship between the respondent and Ye Hongbin was one of nominee shareholding. Although Ye Hongbin agreed in the shareholders' meeting minutes to the respondent's disclosure as a shareholder and to handle the equity change registration, this has no legal effect on others, including Zhengda Company. (3) The shareholders' meeting minutes stated that "the above registration shall be completed before November 15, 2013." The respondent's filing of this lawsuit exceeded the statutory statute of limitations. This case is not a dispute over confirmation of shareholder qualification, but a dispute over whether Ye Hongbin and Jinding Company should perform the obligation of equity change registration. (4) The judgment of the second instance violated the will of Zhengda Company, and there is no essential difference from ordering Zhengda Company to bear civil liability. The court of second instance erred in finding that Zhengda Company had no right to appeal. (5) Relevant facts of this case have not been ascertained, such as whether the respondent actually made capital contributions and whether he performed the debt obligations corresponding to 20% of the shares of Jinding Company. Accordingly, Jinding Company and Zhengda Company, pursuant to Items (2) and (6) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, requested this Court to: revoke the judgments of first and second instance, amend the judgment to dismiss the respondent's claims, or remand the case for retrial.

The respondent submitted opinions, stating: (1) Article 4, paragraph 1 of the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Foreign Investment Law) provides: "The State implements a system of pre-establishment national treatment plus negative list management for foreign investment." Pursuant to this paragraph and Articles 24, 28, 29, and 31 of the Foreign Investment Law, the provision in Article 14, Item (3) of the Provisions (I) should be understood as not requiring all change registrations for the disclosure of nominee shareholders of foreign-invested enterprises to obtain the consent of the foreign-invested enterprise approval authority. After the judgment of second instance, the respondent has already registered the shares in question without being required to undergo any approval procedures. (2) The respondent's request to confirm his shareholder status holding 20% of the shares of Jinding Company and to register his name does not require the consent of Zhengda Company. (a) At the time the shareholders' meeting minutes were formed and when the respondent filed this lawsuit, Zhengda Company was not a shareholder of Jinding Company; (b) In accordance with the principle of transfer of rights and obligations together, Zhengda Company should continue to perform the obligations of the original shareholder of the shares it acquired; (c) The effective rulings of this Court, including Civil Ruling (2017) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 3988 (hereinafter referred to as Ruling No. 3988), and the civil judgments of the court of second instance (2016) Su Min Zhong No. 1220 (hereinafter referred to as Judgment No. 1220) and (2016) Su Min Zhong No. 1463 (hereinafter referred to as Judgment No. 1463), all confirmed that the respondent holds shares of Jinding Company, and Zhengda Company was aware of and acknowledged this. (3) The industrial and commercial registration of the shares in question is a continuing legal obligation of Jinding Company, and the statute of limitations does not apply. On August 18, 2015, the respondent sent a contact letter to Ye Hongbin through the third party Wu Liping, requesting the performance of the change registration obligation within 30 days. Ye Hongbin replied, constituting an interruption of the statute of limitations. (4) The courts of first and second instance did not order Zhengda Company to bear civil liability, and Zhengda Company has no right to apply for retrial.

Upon review, this Court further finds the following facts related to the issues in dispute:

Jinding Company is a limited liability company (joint venture between Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau and domestic parties), with its business scope being real estate development (subject to qualification requirements).

On April 8, 2021, Ye Hongbin issued a "Statement on the Current Shareholding Status of Rugao Jinding Real Estate Co., Ltd.," which states: "In September 2005, the registered shareholders were Ye Hongbin 99.9% and Dadi Company 0.1%; on October 18, 2018, the registered shareholders were Zhengda Company 66.7% and Ye Hongbin 33.3%; on January 27, 2021, the registered shareholders were Zhengda Company 66.7%, Ye Hongbin 13.3%, and the respondent 20%. The 20% currently registered in the respondent's name was transferred upon execution after the court judgment ordering the respondent's disclosure as a shareholder."

The respondent submitted a "Contact Letter" sent to Ye Hongbin on August 11, 2015, via the email of the third party Wu Liping. The letter states: "The shareholders' meeting minutes have clarified the shareholding ratios of each actual shareholder, and you, as the nominee shareholder, have explicitly agreed to handle the industrial and commercial registration change, transferring the shares registered in your name to each actual owner or a wholly-owned company established by the actual owners, in accordance with the ratios confirmed in the resolution, to be completed before November 15, 2013." The respondent also submitted the reply letters from Jinding Company and Ye Hongbin. With respect to the foregoing evidence, Jinding Company and Ye Hongbin did not raise any objection or submit any contrary evidence within the time limit specified by this Court.

This Court is of the opinion that, based on the grounds for retrial and the respondent's opinions, the issues in dispute in this case are: (1) Whether the re-applicants' claim that the equity change registration in question should have obtained the consent of the foreign-invested enterprise approval authority is sustainable? (2) Whether the re-applicants' claim that the court of second instance erred in failing to consider Zhengda Company's opinions regarding the equity change registration is sustainable?

I. Whether the re-applicants' claim that the equity change registration in question should have obtained the consent of the foreign-invested enterprise approval authority is sustainable.

Article 4, paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Foreign Investment Law provide: "The State implements a system of pre-establishment national treatment plus negative list management for foreign investment. The pre-establishment national treatment referred to in the preceding paragraph means the treatment accorded to foreign investors and their investments, in the investment admission stage, that is no less favorable than that accorded to domestic investors and their investments; the negative list referred to means the special management measures for the admission of foreign investment in specific fields as prescribed by the State. The State grants national treatment to foreign investment outside the negative list." Article 28, paragraph 3 of the Foreign Investment Law provides: "Fields other than those on the negative list for foreign investment admission shall be managed in accordance with the principle of equal treatment for domestic and foreign investment." Article 31 provides: "The organizational form, organizational structure, and operational rules of foreign-invested enterprises shall be governed by the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, the Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant laws." Pursuant to Article 48, paragraph 1 of the Implementing Regulations of the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Implementing Regulations of the Foreign Investment Law), if laws, administrative regulations, or the State Council provide otherwise, those provisions shall prevail; otherwise, investors from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region making investments in the Mainland shall be governed by reference to the Foreign Investment Law and its implementing regulations.

In this case, the shareholders' meeting minutes confirmed that the respondent holds 20% of the shares of Jinding Company and specified that the equity change registration should be completed before November 15, 2013. At that time, Article 3 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures (hereinafter referred to as the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Law) then in effect provided: "The joint venture agreement, contract, and articles of association signed by the parties shall be submitted to the competent department for foreign economic relations and trade for examination and approval." Article 15 of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Law as amended in 2016 provided: "For the establishment of a joint venture that does not involve special management measures for admission implemented by the State, the approval matters provided for in Articles 3, 13, and 14 of this Law shall be subject to record-filing management." During the trial of the court of second instance, the Foreign Investment Law, the Implementing Regulations of the Foreign Investment Law, and the Measures for Foreign Investment Information Reporting formulated by the Ministry of Commerce and the State Administration for Market Regulation came into effect on January 1, 2020, establishing a system of pre-establishment national treatment plus negative list management and foreign investment information reporting for foreign investment. With respect to fields outside the negative list, Article 4 of the Foreign Investment Law provides for "granting national treatment," and Article 28, paragraph 3 provides: "management in accordance with the principle of equal treatment for domestic and foreign investment."

After the Foreign Investment Law and its implementing regulations came into effect, the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Law, the Law of the People's Republic of China on Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises, the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Contractual Joint Ventures, and their respective implementing regulations or detailed rules were simultaneously abolished. The systems of examination, approval, and record-filing management in these abolished laws and administrative regulations are no longer implemented. Therefore, even if the relevant legal act occurred before the implementation of the Foreign Investment Law, if the equity change registration of the foreign-invested enterprise in dispute does not fall within the scope of the negative list as referred to in Article 4 of the Foreign Investment Law, the people's court shall not support the party's claim that the consent of the foreign-invested enterprise approval authority should have been obtained, in accordance with the principles of "granting national treatment" and "equal treatment of domestic and foreign investment." In this case, the business scope of Jinding Company is "real estate development," and the equity change registration in question does not fall within the scope of the negative list. Therefore, the relevant ground for retrial of the re-applicants cannot be sustained.

II. Whether the re-applicants' claim that the court of second instance erred in failing to consider Zhengda Company's opinions regarding the equity change registration is sustainable.

Article 22 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (III) provides: "Where a dispute arises between the parties over the ownership of equity, and a party requests the people's court to confirm that it holds the equity, it shall prove one of the following facts: (1) it has made capital contributions or subscribed for capital contributions to the company in accordance with the law, and does not violate mandatory provisions of laws or regulations; (2) it has acquired the company's equity by transfer or other means, and does not violate mandatory provisions of laws or regulations." Article 23 provides: "Where a party, after fulfilling its capital contribution obligations or acquiring the equity by succession in accordance with the law, the company fails to issue a capital contribution certificate, record it in the register of shareholders, and register it with the company registration authority in accordance with Articles 32 and 33 of the Company Law, and the party requests the company to perform the above obligations, the people's court shall support such request." In this case, based on evidence such as the shareholders' meeting minutes and the "Share Confirmation Letter" dated October 20, 2013, it can be proven that the respondent has actually made investments and holds 20% of the shares of Jinding Company. The respondent, as authorized by Ye Hongbin, chaired the shareholders' meeting, jointly recommended directors with other shareholders, and has actually participated in the company's operational management activities, exercising shareholder rights. The respondent filed this lawsuit on June 26, 2017, and Zhengda Company acquired Ye Hongbin's shares of Jinding Company on October 18, 2018. Based on the findings of the effective Ruling No. 3988, Judgment No. 1220, and Judgment No. 1463, the re-applicants' claim that the court of second instance erred in failing to consider Zhengda Company's opinions cannot be sustained.

In August 2015, the respondent sent a contact letter via the email of the third party Wu Liping, requesting Ye Hongbin and Jinding Company to handle the equity change registration in accordance with the shareholders' meeting minutes. The re-applicants' ground for retrial that the statute of limitations had expired cannot be sustained. Zhengda Company was a third party without independent claims in the first instance. The equity change registration in question does not involve the equity held by Zhengda Company, and the judgment of first instance did not order it to bear legal liability. Therefore, Zhengda Company's ground for retrial that it had the right to appeal also cannot be sustained.

In conclusion, the retrial applications of Jinding Company and Zhengda Company do not meet the circumstances provided for in Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 204, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 395, paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled as follows:

The retrial applications of Rugao Jinding Real Estate Co., Ltd. and Nantong Zhengda Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. are rejected.
